title: Inequality Measurement, Decomposition, and Poverty Analysis
text: main CRAN package inequality measurement (ineq) last updated 2014. computes basic Gini Theil indices support survey weights, confidence intervals, subgroup decomposition, poverty measures, Palma ratio, tax progressivity analysis. inequality fills gaps. bring income wealth data source (household surveys, tax records, administrative data, simulations) package handles measurement, decomposition, comparison. what: inequality: Inequality Measurement, Decomposition, and Poverty Analysis — inequality-package
title: inequality: Inequality Measurement, Decomposition, and Poverty Analysis — inequality-package
text: Tools measuring income wealth inequality. Computes Gini coefficient bootstrap asymptotic confidence intervals following Davidson (2009) doi:10.1016/j.jeconom.2008.11.004 , extended S-Gini family, Theil T L indices (generalised entropy family), Atkinson index, Kolm absolute inequality index, Palma ratio, Hoover index, percentile ratios, Lorenz curves. Supports -within group decomposition following Bourguignon (1979) doi:10.2307/1914138 , income share tabulation, concentration indices health inequality Erreygers (2009) correction, Kakwani tax progressivity Reynolds-Smolensky redistribution indices, Foster-Greer-Thorbecke poverty measures including Sen index, growth incidence curves following Ravallion Chen (2003) doi:10.1016/S0165-1765(02)00205-7 , Wolfson polarisation. functions accept optional survey weights work data source.

title: Atkinson index — iq_atkinson
text: Computes Atkinson inequality index, incorporates explicit normative judgement inequality aversion parameter epsilon. Higher epsilon gives weight transfers bottom distribution.

title: Atkinson index — iq_atkinson
code: iq_atkinson(x, weights = NULL, epsilon = 0.5, na.rm = FALSE)

title: Atkinson index — iq_atkinson
text: x Numeric vector incomes (strictly positive). weights Optional numeric vector survey weights. epsilon Numeric. Inequality aversion parameter (> 0). Default 0.5. Common values: 0.5 (moderate), 1.0 (high), 2.0 (high aversion). na.rm Logical. Remove NA values? Default FALSE.

title: Atkinson index — iq_atkinson
text: S3 object class "iq_atkinson" elements: value Numeric. Atkinson index (0 1). epsilon Numeric. inequality aversion parameter used. ede Numeric. equally distributed equivalent income. mean_income Numeric. mean income. n Integer. Number observations.

title: Atkinson index — iq_atkinson
text: Atkinson, . B. (1970). "Measurement Inequality." Journal Economic Theory, 2(3), 244–263.

title: Atkinson index — iq_atkinson
code: d <- iq_sample_data("income")  # Moderate inequality aversion iq_atkinson(d$income, epsilon = 0.5) #>  #> ── Atkinson Index ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> • Value: 0.1506 #> • Epsilon: 0.5 #> • EDE income: 41783.21 #> • Mean income: 49190.12 #> • Observations: 1000  # High inequality aversion iq_atkinson(d$income, epsilon = 1) #>  #> ── Atkinson Index ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> • Value: 0.2768 #> • Epsilon: 1 #> • EDE income: 35572.94 #> • Mean income: 49190.12 #> • Observations: 1000  # Very high inequality aversion iq_atkinson(d$income, epsilon = 2) #>  #> ── Atkinson Index ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> • Value: 0.4765 #> • Epsilon: 2 #> • EDE income: 25750.78 #> • Mean income: 49190.12 #> • Observations: 1000

title: Concentration index — iq_concentration
text: Computes concentration index, measures inequality health () variable across income distribution. Unlike Gini coefficient, ranking variable outcome variable different.

title: Concentration index — iq_concentration
code: iq_concentration(   x,   rank,   weights = NULL,   correction = c("none", "erreygers"),   bounds = c(0, 1),   na.rm = FALSE )

title: Concentration index — iq_concentration
text: x Numeric vector outcome values (e.g. health expenditure). rank Numeric vector ranking values (e.g. income). Must length x. weights Optional numeric vector survey weights. correction Character. "none" (default) standard index, "erreygers" Erreygers (2009) correction bounded variables. bounds Numeric vector length 2 giving lower upper bounds x. Required correction = "erreygers". Default c(0, 1) (suitable binary proportion variables). na.rm Logical. Remove NA values? Default FALSE.

title: Concentration index — iq_concentration
text: S3 object class "iq_concentration" elements: value Numeric. concentration index. correction Character. correction applied. n Integer. Number observations.

title: Concentration index — iq_concentration
text: positive value indicates outcome concentrated among better-; negative value indicates concentration among worse-. bounded variables (e.g. binary health indicators), standard concentration index bounds depend mean. Use correction = "erreygers" Erreygers (2009) corrected index, fixed bounds -1 1 regardless mean.

title: Concentration index — iq_concentration
text: Wagstaff, ., Paci, P. van Doorslaer, E. (1991). "Measurement Inequalities Health." Social Science Medicine, 33(5), 545–557. Erreygers, G. (2009). "Correcting Concentration Index." Journal Health Economics, 28(2), 504–515.

title: Concentration index — iq_concentration
code: set.seed(1) income <- rlnorm(200, 10, 0.8) health_exp <- income * 0.05 + rnorm(200, 500, 100) iq_concentration(health_exp, rank = income) #>  #> ── Concentration Index ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> • Value: 0.3065 #> • Observations: 200  # Binary outcome with Erreygers correction sick <- as.numeric(income < median(income)) + rbinom(200, 1, 0.1) sick <- pmin(sick, 1) iq_concentration(sick, rank = income, correction = "erreygers") #>  #> ── Concentration Index (Erreygers) ───────────────────────────────────────────── #> • Value: -0.8826 #> • Observations: 200

title: Between-within group decomposition — iq_decompose
text: Decomposes generalised entropy index -group component (inequality due differences group means) within-group component (inequality within group). decomposition exact: + within = total.

title: Between-within group decomposition — iq_decompose
code: iq_decompose(x, group, weights = NULL, index = "T", na.rm = FALSE)

title: Between-within group decomposition — iq_decompose
text: x Numeric vector incomes (strictly positive). group Factor character vector identifying group membership. weights Optional numeric vector survey weights. index Character numeric. "T" Theil T (GE(1)), "L" mean log deviation (GE(0)), numeric alpha. Default "T". na.rm Logical. Remove NA values? Default FALSE.

title: Between-within group decomposition — iq_decompose
text: S3 object class "iq_decomposition" elements: total Numeric. total GE index. Numeric. -group component. within Numeric. within-group component. groups data.frame columns group, n, mean_income, pop_share, income_share, within_ge. index_name Character. Name index used.

title: Between-within group decomposition — iq_decompose
text: Bourguignon, F. (1979). "Decomposable Income Inequality Measures." Econometrica, 47(4), 901–920.

title: Between-within group decomposition — iq_decompose
code: d <- iq_sample_data("grouped") iq_decompose(d$income, d$group) #>  #> ── Between-Within Decomposition (Theil T (GE(1))) ────────────────────────────── #> • Total: 0.463 #> • Between: 0.116 (25.1%) #> • Within: 0.347 (74.9%) #>  #> ── Group Detail ── #>  #> • A: n=400, mean=31572, pop=40%, income=24.1% #> • B: n=350, mean=44006, pop=35%, income=29.4% #> • C: n=250, mean=97783, pop=25%, income=46.6%

title: Gini coefficient — iq_gini
text: Computes Gini coefficient distribution, optional survey weights confidence intervals (bootstrap asymptotic).

title: Gini coefficient — iq_gini
code: iq_gini(   x,   weights = NULL,   na.rm = FALSE,   ci = FALSE,   method = c("bootstrap", "asymptotic"),   R = 1000L,   level = 0.95 )

title: Gini coefficient — iq_gini
text: x Numeric vector incomes values (non-negative). weights Optional numeric vector survey weights. na.rm Logical. Remove NA values? Default FALSE. ci Logical. Compute confidence intervals? Default FALSE. method Character. CI method: "bootstrap" (default) "asymptotic" (jackknife-based, faster large samples). R Integer. Number bootstrap replicates (ignored asymptotic). Default 1000. level Numeric. Confidence level. Default 0.95.

title: Gini coefficient — iq_gini
text: S3 object class "iq_gini" elements: gini Numeric. Gini coefficient. n Integer. Number observations. se Numeric NULL. Standard error (asymptotic method ). ci_lower Numeric NULL. Lower bound CI. ci_upper Numeric NULL. Upper bound CI. level Numeric NULL. Confidence level. method Character NULL. CI method used.

title: Gini coefficient — iq_gini
text: Gini coefficient ranges 0 (perfect equality) 1 (perfect inequality). equals twice area Lorenz curve 45-degree line.

title: Gini coefficient — iq_gini
text: Gini, C. (1912). "Variabilita e mutabilita." Reprinted Memorie di metodologica statistica (Ed. Pizetti E, Salvemini, T). Rome: Libreria Eredi Virgilio Veschi. Davidson, R. (2009). "Reliable Inference Gini Index." Journal Econometrics, 150(1), 30–40.

title: Gini coefficient — iq_gini
code: d <- iq_sample_data("income") iq_gini(d$income) #>  #> ── Gini Coefficient ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> • Gini: 0.43 #> • Observations: 1000  # Bootstrap CIs iq_gini(d$income, ci = TRUE, R = 500) #>  #> ── Gini Coefficient ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> • Gini: 0.43 #> • Observations: 1000 #> • Bootstrap 95% CI: [0.4068, 0.4541]  # Asymptotic CIs (faster for large samples) iq_gini(d$income, ci = TRUE, method = "asymptotic") #>  #> ── Gini Coefficient ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> • Gini: 0.43 #> • Observations: 1000 #> • Asymptotic 95% CI: [0.4065, 0.4534]  # Perfect equality iq_gini(rep(100, 50)) #>  #> ── Gini Coefficient ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> • Gini: 0 #> • Observations: 50

title: Growth incidence curve — iq_growth_incidence
text: Computes growth incidence curve (GIC), showing annualised total growth rate quantile distribution two time periods.

title: Growth incidence curve — iq_growth_incidence
code: iq_growth_incidence(   x_t0,   x_t1,   weights_t0 = NULL,   weights_t1 = NULL,   n_quantiles = 20L,   na.rm = FALSE )

title: Growth incidence curve — iq_growth_incidence
text: x_t0 Numeric vector incomes period 0. x_t1 Numeric vector incomes period 1. Must length x_t0. weights_t0 Optional weights period 0. weights_t1 Optional weights period 1. n_quantiles Integer. Number quantile bins. Default 20 (ventiles). na.rm Logical. Remove NA values? Default FALSE.

title: Growth incidence curve — iq_growth_incidence
text: S3 object class "iq_growth_incidence" elements: gic data.frame columns quantile (midpoint), growth (proportional growth rate quantile). mean_growth Numeric. Mean growth across quantiles. median_growth Numeric. Median growth rate. n_quantiles Integer.

title: Growth incidence curve — iq_growth_incidence
text: GIC upward-sloping, rich grew faster inequality increased. downward-sloping, growth pro-poor.

title: Growth incidence curve — iq_growth_incidence
text: Ravallion, M. Chen, S. (2003). "Measuring Pro-Poor Growth." Economics Letters, 78(1), 93–99.

title: Growth incidence curve — iq_growth_incidence
code: d <- iq_sample_data("panel") gic <- iq_growth_incidence(d$income_t0, d$income_t1) plot(gic)

title: Hoover index (Robin Hood index) — iq_hoover
text: Computes Hoover index, also known Robin Hood index Schutz coefficient. equals maximum proportion total income need redistributed achieve perfect equality, equivalently, half mean absolute deviation divided mean.

title: Hoover index (Robin Hood index) — iq_hoover
code: iq_hoover(x, weights = NULL, na.rm = FALSE)

title: Hoover index (Robin Hood index) — iq_hoover
text: x Numeric vector incomes (non-negative). weights Optional numeric vector survey weights. na.rm Logical. Remove NA values? Default FALSE.

title: Hoover index (Robin Hood index) — iq_hoover
text: S3 object class "iq_hoover" elements: value Numeric. Hoover index (0 1). n Integer. Number observations.

title: Kakwani progressivity index — iq_kakwani
text: Measures progressivity tax transfer system. positive value indicates progressivity (rich pay larger share income share); negative value indicates regressivity. Zero means proportional.

title: Kakwani progressivity index — iq_kakwani
code: iq_kakwani(pre_tax, tax, weights = NULL, na.rm = FALSE)

title: Kakwani progressivity index — iq_kakwani
text: pre_tax Numeric vector pre-tax incomes (non-negative). tax Numeric vector tax payments (length pre_tax). Positive values taxes paid; negative values transfers received. weights Optional numeric vector survey weights. na.rm Logical. Remove NA values? Default FALSE.

title: Kakwani progressivity index — iq_kakwani
text: S3 object class "iq_kakwani" elements: kakwani Numeric. Kakwani index (-1 1). gini_pre Numeric. pre-tax Gini coefficient. concentration_tax Numeric. concentration coefficient taxes. reynolds_smolensky Numeric. Reynolds-Smolensky index (pre-tax Gini minus post-tax Gini). gini_post Numeric. post-tax Gini coefficient. avg_tax_rate Numeric. Average effective tax rate. n Integer. Number observations.

title: Kakwani progressivity index — iq_kakwani
text: Kakwani index equals concentration coefficient tax minus pre-tax Gini coefficient: K = C_T - G_pre.

title: Kakwani progressivity index — iq_kakwani
text: Kakwani, N. C. (1977). "Measurement Tax Progressivity: International Comparison." Economic Journal, 87(345), 71–80. Reynolds, M. Smolensky, E. (1977). Public Expenditures, Taxes, Distribution Income. New York: Academic Press.

title: Kakwani progressivity index — iq_kakwani
code: set.seed(1) pre <- iq_sample_data("income")$income # Progressive tax: higher rate for higher incomes tax <- pre * (0.10 + 0.15 * (pre / max(pre))) iq_kakwani(pre, tax) #>  #> ── Fiscal Progressivity (Progressive) ────────────────────────────────────────── #> • Kakwani index: 0.0646 #> • Reynolds-Smolensky index: 0.0092 #> • Pre-tax Gini: 0.43 #> • Post-tax Gini: 0.4208 #> • Tax concentration coefficient: 0.4946 #> • Average tax rate: 12.5% #> • Observations: 1000

title: Kolm index (absolute inequality) — iq_kolm
text: Computes Kolm index, standard inequality measure translation-invariant (absolute). Adding amount every income leaves index unchanged. indices package scale-invariant (relative): multiplying every income factor leaves unchanged.

title: Kolm index (absolute inequality) — iq_kolm
code: iq_kolm(x, weights = NULL, alpha = 1, na.rm = FALSE)

title: Kolm index (absolute inequality) — iq_kolm
text: x Numeric vector incomes. weights Optional numeric vector survey weights. alpha Numeric. Inequality aversion parameter (> 0). Default 1. na.rm Logical. Remove NA values? Default FALSE.

title: Kolm index (absolute inequality) — iq_kolm
text: S3 object class "iq_kolm" elements: value Numeric. Kolm index. alpha Numeric. inequality aversion parameter used. n Integer. Number observations.

title: Kolm index (absolute inequality) — iq_kolm
text: Higher alpha gives weight inequality bottom distribution. index always non-negative equals zero perfect equality.

title: Kolm index (absolute inequality) — iq_kolm
text: Kolm, S.-C. (1976). "Unequal Inequalities II." Journal Economic Theory, 13(1), 82–111.

title: Kolm index (absolute inequality) — iq_kolm
code: d <- iq_sample_data("income") iq_kolm(d$income, alpha = 1) #>  #> ── Kolm Index (absolute inequality) ──────────────────────────────────────────── #> • Value: 46736.2301 #> • Alpha: 1 #> • Observations: 1000  # Higher aversion to inequality at the bottom iq_kolm(d$income, alpha = 2) #>  #> ── Kolm Index (absolute inequality) ──────────────────────────────────────────── #> • Value: 46739.684 #> • Alpha: 2 #> • Observations: 1000

title: Palma ratio — iq_palma

title: Palma ratio — iq_palma
text: Palma ratio motivated Palma's (2011) observation "middle" 50 percent (deciles 5–9) tends capture remarkably stable share income across countries, inequality driven happens tails. Palma ratio 1 means top 10 percent bottom 40 percent receive equal shares.

title: Palma ratio — iq_palma
text: Palma, J. G. (2011). "Homogeneous Middles vs. Heterogeneous Tails, End 'Inverted-U': Share Rich." Development Change, 42(1), 87–153.

title: Percentile ratio — iq_percentile_ratio

text: S3 object class "iq_percentile_ratio" elements: ratio Numeric. percentile ratio. upper_value Numeric. value upper percentile. lower_value Numeric. value lower percentile. upper Numeric. upper percentile used. lower Numeric. lower percentile used. n Integer. Number observations.

title: Polarisation index — iq_polarisation
text: Computes Wolfson bipolarisation index, measures extent distribution bimodal (clustering tails) rather unimodal. Higher values indicate polarisation.

title: Polarisation index — iq_polarisation
code: iq_polarisation(x, weights = NULL, na.rm = FALSE)

title: Polarisation index — iq_polarisation
text: x Numeric vector incomes (non-negative). weights Optional numeric vector survey weights. na.rm Logical. Remove NA values? Default FALSE.

title: Polarisation index — iq_polarisation
text: S3 object class "iq_polarisation" elements: wolfson Numeric. Wolfson polarisation index. gini Numeric. Gini coefficient. median Numeric. weighted median income. mean Numeric. weighted mean income. n Integer. Number observations.

title: Polarisation index — iq_polarisation

title: Polarisation index — iq_polarisation
code: d <- iq_sample_data("income") iq_polarisation(d$income) #>  #> ── Polarisation ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> • Wolfson index: 0.1988 #> • Gini: 0.43 #> • Median income: 35934.96 #> • Mean income: 49190.12 #> • Observations: 1000

title: Poverty measures — iq_poverty
text: Computes Foster-Greer-Thorbecke (FGT) family poverty measures, plus Sen index Watts index. measures require poverty line.

title: Poverty measures — iq_poverty
code: iq_poverty(x, line, weights = NULL, na.rm = FALSE)

title: Poverty measures — iq_poverty
text: x Numeric vector incomes (non-negative). line Numeric. poverty line. Required. weights Optional numeric vector survey weights. na.rm Logical. Remove NA values? Default FALSE.

title: Poverty measures — iq_poverty
text: S3 object class "iq_poverty" elements: headcount Numeric. FGT(0): proportion poverty line. gap Numeric. FGT(1): average normalised gap. severity Numeric. FGT(2): average squared normalised gap. sen Numeric. Sen index: headcount * (gap among poor + Gini among poor * (1 - gap among poor)). watts Numeric. Watts index: mean log(line/x) among poor. line Numeric. poverty line used. n Integer. Number observations. n_poor Integer. Number observations line.

title: Poverty measures — iq_poverty
text: Foster, J., Greer, J. Thorbecke, E. (1984). "Class Decomposable Poverty Measures." Econometrica, 52(3), 761–766. Sen, . (1976). "Poverty: Ordinal Approach Measurement." Econometrica, 44(2), 219–231.

title: Poverty measures — iq_poverty
code: d <- iq_sample_data("income") # Poverty line at the 20th percentile p20 <- quantile(d$income, 0.20) iq_poverty(d$income, line = p20) #>  #> ── Poverty Measures (line = 17977.94) ────────────────────────────────────────── #> • Headcount (FGT0): 20% #> • Poverty gap (FGT1): 0.0639 #> • Severity (FGT2): 0.029 #> • Sen index: 0.0874 #> • Watts index: 0.0891 #> • Poor: 200 of 1000 observations

title: Generate sample inequality data — iq_sample_data
text: Creates synthetic data testing demonstrating inequalitykit functions. Three types available: individual incomes, two-period panel growth incidence analysis, grouped incomes decomposition.

title: Generate sample inequality data — iq_sample_data
code: iq_sample_data(type = c("income", "panel", "grouped"))

title: Generate sample inequality data — iq_sample_data
text: type Character. One "income", "panel", "grouped".

title: Generate sample inequality data — iq_sample_data
text: data.frame. "income" 1000 rows columns income weight. Drawn lognormal distribution (mean log 10.5, sd log 0.8), producing realistic income-like data centred around 40,000. "panel" 1000 rows columns income_t0, income_t1, weight. Two periods heterogeneous growth (bottom grows slower top, mimicking rising inequality). "grouped" 1000 rows columns income, group, weight. Three groups (, B, C) different mean incomes /within decomposition.

title: S-Gini (extended Gini family) — iq_sgini
text: Computes S-Gini coefficient, one-parameter generalisation Gini allows user specify much weight give different parts distribution. standard Gini special case delta = 2.

title: S-Gini (extended Gini family) — iq_sgini
code: iq_sgini(x, weights = NULL, delta = 2, na.rm = FALSE)

title: S-Gini (extended Gini family) — iq_sgini
text: x Numeric vector incomes (non-negative). weights Optional numeric vector survey weights. delta Numeric. Inequality aversion parameter (> 1). Default 2 (standard Gini). na.rm Logical. Remove NA values? Default FALSE.

title: S-Gini (extended Gini family) — iq_sgini
text: S3 object class "iq_sgini" elements: value Numeric. S-Gini coefficient. delta Numeric. inequality aversion parameter used. n Integer. Number observations.

title: S-Gini (extended Gini family) — iq_sgini
text: Lower delta (approaching 1) gives equal weight everywhere; higher delta gives weight bottom distribution. standard Gini (delta = 2) weights rank position. Delta = 3 4 places even emphasis poorest.

title: S-Gini (extended Gini family) — iq_sgini
text: Donaldson, D. Weymark, J. . (1980). "Single-Parameter Generalization Gini Indices Inequality." Journal Economic Theory, 22(1), 67–86. Yitzhaki, S. (1983). "Extension Gini Inequality Index." International Economic Review, 24(3), 617–628.

title: S-Gini (extended Gini family) — iq_sgini
code: d <- iq_sample_data("income")  # Standard Gini (delta = 2) iq_sgini(d$income, delta = 2) #>  #> ── S-Gini (standard Gini, delta = 2) ─────────────────────────────────────────── #> • Value: 0.43 #> • Observations: 1000  # More weight on the bottom of the distribution iq_sgini(d$income, delta = 3) #>  #> ── S-Gini (delta = 3) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> • Value: 0.5627 #> • Observations: 1000

title: Income shares by quantile — iq_shares
text: Computes share total income held segment distribution. Default segments: bottom 50%, middle 40%, top 10%, top 1%.

title: Income shares by quantile — iq_shares
code: iq_shares(x, weights = NULL, breaks = c(0.5, 0.9, 0.99, 1), na.rm = FALSE)

title: Income shares by quantile — iq_shares
text: x Numeric vector incomes (non-negative). weights Optional numeric vector survey weights. breaks Numeric vector cumulative population thresholds defining segments. Default c(0.50, 0.90, 0.99, 1.00). na.rm Logical. Remove NA values? Default FALSE.

title: Income shares by quantile — iq_shares
text: S3 object class "iq_shares" elements: shares data.frame columns segment, pop_share, income_share. n Integer. Number observations.

title: Income shares by quantile — iq_shares
code: d <- iq_sample_data("income") iq_shares(d$income) #>  #> ── Income Shares ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> • Bottom 50%: 21.2% of income (50% of population) #> • P50-P90: 47.2% of income (40% of population) #> • P90-P99: 24.2% of income (9% of population) #> • Top 1%: 7.3% of income (1% of population) #> • Observations: 1000  # Custom breaks: quintiles iq_shares(d$income, breaks = c(0.20, 0.40, 0.60, 0.80, 1.00)) #>  #> ── Income Shares ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> • Bottom 20%: 5% of income (20% of population) #> • P20-P40: 9.7% of income (20% of population) #> • P40-P60: 14.5% of income (20% of population) #> • P60-P80: 22.4% of income (20% of population) #> • Top 20%: 48.5% of income (20% of population) #> • Observations: 1000

what: Theil index and generalised entropy measures — iq_theil
title: Theil index and generalised entropy measures — iq_theil
text: Computes Theil T index (GE(1)), Theil L / mean log deviation (GE(0)), generalised entropy index GE(alpha) non-negative alpha.

title: Theil index and generalised entropy measures — iq_theil
code: iq_theil(x, weights = NULL, index = "T", na.rm = FALSE)

title: Theil index and generalised entropy measures — iq_theil
text: x Numeric vector incomes (strictly positive). weights Optional numeric vector survey weights. index Character numeric. "T" Theil T (GE(1)), "L" mean log deviation (GE(0)), numeric value GE(alpha). Default "T". na.rm Logical. Remove NA values? Default FALSE.

title: Theil index and generalised entropy measures — iq_theil
text: S3 object class "iq_theil" elements: value Numeric. index value. alpha Numeric. alpha parameter used. index_name Character. Human-readable name index. n Integer. Number observations.

title: Theil index and generalised entropy measures — iq_theil
text: Generalised entropy indices class inequality measures decomposable population subgroups satisfy transfer principle. Higher values indicate inequality.

title: Theil index and generalised entropy measures — iq_theil
text: Theil, H. (1967). Economics Information Theory. Amsterdam: North-Holland. Cowell, F. . (2011). Measuring Inequality. 3rd edition. Oxford University Press. Shorrocks, . F. (1980). "Class Additively Decomposable Inequality Measures." Econometrica, 48(3), 613–625.

title: Theil index and generalised entropy measures — iq_theil
code: d <- iq_sample_data("income")  # Theil T (GE(1)) iq_theil(d$income, index = "T") #>  #> ── Theil T (GE(1)) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> • Value: 0.3307 #> • Observations: 1000  # Mean log deviation (GE(0)) iq_theil(d$income, index = "L") #>  #> ── Theil L / Mean Log Deviation (GE(0)) ──────────────────────────────────────── #> • Value: 0.3241 #> • Observations: 1000  # GE(2): half the squared coefficient of variation iq_theil(d$income, index = 2) #>  #> ── GE(2) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> • Value: 0.4951 #> • Observations: 1000

text: CRAN release: 2026-04-20 Initial release.

title: inequality 0.1.0
text: Gini coefficient bootstrap asymptotic (jackknife) confidence intervals via iq_gini(), following Davidson (2009). Extended S-Gini family adjustable inequality aversion parameter via iq_sgini(), following Donaldson Weymark (1980). Theil T (GE(1)), mean log deviation (GE(0)), general GE(alpha) via iq_theil(), following Theil (1967) Shorrocks (1980). Atkinson index inequality aversion parameter via iq_atkinson(). Kolm absolute inequality index via iq_kolm(). Palma ratio (top 10% / bottom 40% income shares) via iq_palma(). Hoover index (Robin Hood / Pietra index) via iq_hoover(). Percentile ratios (P90/P10, P80/P20, custom) via iq_percentile_ratio().

title: inequality 0.1.0
text: Lorenz curve base graphics plot method via iq_lorenz(). -within group decomposition generalised entropy family via iq_decompose(), following Bourguignon (1979). Income share tabulation (bottom 50%, middle 40%, top 10%, top 1%) via iq_shares(). Concentration index health inequality optional Erreygers (2009) correction via iq_concentration(). Wolfson bipolarisation index via iq_polarisation().

title: inequality 0.1.0
text: Foster-Greer-Thorbecke poverty measures (headcount, gap, severity), Sen index, Watts index via iq_poverty(). Growth incidence curve plot method via iq_growth_incidence(), following Ravallion Chen (2003).

title: inequality 0.1.0
text: Kakwani progressivity index Reynolds-Smolensky redistribution index via iq_kakwani().

title: inequality 0.1.0
text: Side--side comparison major indices via iq_compare(). functions accept optional survey weights.
